test_title: PYST 2: SSC CHSL 2023 - Quantitative Aptitude(Held On: 02 Aug, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A publisher supplies books to a book - seller at a 20% discount on the list price of Rs. 1,574.80. If the book - seller sells books at the list price and if his expenses for freight etc. are Rs. 45.40, determine his profit.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In this case, since the **Selling Price** is equal to the **List Price**, the **Gross Profit** is simply the **Discount** amount.

**Net Profit** = **Discount** − **Expenses**

**Discount** = 20% of 1,574.80 = 314.96

**Net Profit** = 314.96 − 45.40 = 269.56

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 269.56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**List Price** = Rs. 1,574.80

**Discount Rate** = 20%

**Freight Expenses** = Rs. 45.40

**Selling Price** = **List Price**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/41cf58ec792b904c0ea273497c7c6c494ae97dde27b654bf23e192be184635c5.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Purchase Price** = **List Price** − **Discount**

**Total Cost Price** = **Purchase Price** + **Expenses**

**Profit** = **Selling Price** − **Total Cost Price**

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Discount** = 20% of 1,574.80

⇒ **Discount** = (20 ÷ 100) × 1,574.80 = 314.96

⇒ **Purchase Price** = 1,574.80 − 314.96 = 1,259.84

⇒ **Total Cost Price** = 1,259.84 + 45.40 = 1,305.24

⇒ **Selling Price** = 1,574.80

⇒ **Profit** = 1,574.80 − 1,305.24 = 269.56

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 269.56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Cost Price (Effective CP)

It includes the **Purchase Price** plus all additional overhead expenses such as **freight**, **transportation**, **repairs**, and **labor** charges.

Discount on List Price

**Discount** is always calculated on the **List Price** (or **Marked Price**) unless specified otherwise. Net Price = LP × (100 − D)%.

Profit Percentage

**Profit %** = (**Profit** ÷ **Total Cost Price**) × 100. It measures the gain relative to the total investment.</p
